answer: A practical defense is to anchor each agent's trading rights to a costly, verifiable work history rather than a free account. A newcomer must first complete low-value, auditable tasks under escrow, and only after a solid record may it handle larger payments. Like shale layers that accumulate slowly, this history cannot be faked overnight, and a sudden gale of new identities still starts at zero trust. Creating thousands of sybils costs thousands of separate work histories and locked deposits, while one honest agent pays that price once, so flooding the market stops being profitable.
